entries.title: Tummy time when your baby hates it: a gentler start
entries.summary: Why tummy time matters and gentle, supervised ways to try when the mat ends in tears.
entries.brief: Reassuring, useful tummy-time ideas that never treat a milestone as a test.

entries.title: Your baby's relationship with solids: curiosity before clean plates
entries.summary: How to notice readiness, make room for exploration, and keep early meals low-pressure.
entries.brief: Check current CDC, NHS and WHO guidance. Give no individualized feeding or allergen advice.
entries.appNote: If you want to remember what made your baby curious at the table, BabyBaby gives you a place to save a photo and a few words.

entries.title: What a baby's growth curve can—and cannot—tell you
entries.summary: How clinicians use a series of measurements and why one dot rarely tells the whole story.
entries.brief: Explain trends and measurement context without interpreting one child's chart.
entries.appNote: BabyBaby can keep your recorded growth measurements together so you can look at them with your child's care professional.

screenshot.alt: BabyBaby growth chart showing sample weight measurements plotted across months of age
screenshot.caption: A genuine BabyBaby growth view with sample data. It illustrates how measurements appear over time, not a clinical interpretation of one child.

entries.title: A two-minute handover between caregivers
entries.summary: A useful script for passing on the details the next caregiver actually needs.
entries.brief: Give a reusable handover template. Paper or a shared note should work too.
entries.appNote: BabyBaby's Family Sharing can give a partner or caregiver the same view of the daily logs, if your family prefers one shared place.

entries.title: The little conversations before words
entries.summary: Everyday ways to talk, pause, and respond to a baby before they can speak.
entries.brief: Use primary child-development sources on responsive interaction. One optional memory prompt is enough of an app connection.

entries.title: The baby photos worth keeping aren't always milestones
entries.summary: How to capture ordinary moments and the small details that give them meaning later.
entries.brief: Practical memory prompts and photo organization.
entries.appNote: BabyBaby memories let you keep a photo with the words that explain why that ordinary moment mattered.

entries.title: Teething or something else? What to notice
entries.summary: A calm look at common teething questions and when to ask a clinician.
entries.brief: Use current primary pediatric sources, avoid diagnosis and medication recommendations, and direct concerns to a clinician. No product section.

entries.title: When naps change: observe a week without forcing a schedule
entries.summary: A way to look at shifting rest patterns while staying flexible about an individual baby.
entries.brief: Avoid prescribed nap targets and sleep-safety shortcuts.
entries.appNote: BabyBaby's timeline can put the sleep stretches you recorded side by side, making it easier to notice a question to explore.

screenshot.alt: BabyBaby weekly timeline with daily rows and colored sleep stretches
screenshot.caption: A genuine BabyBaby weekly overview using sample entries. Blank spaces may mean something was not recorded; this is not a recommended sleep schedule.

entries.title: Play without a toy haul
entries.summary: Simple, supervised ways to play using safe everyday objects and your attention.
entries.brief: Give low-cost activity ideas with age and safety context. No app pitch.

entries.title: Introducing allergens: questions for your child's clinician
entries.summary: What to ask before starting and how to prepare a useful, individual conversation.
entries.brief: High-stakes topic: provide questions and source links, never an individualized plan or unsupported timing rules. If current authoritative sources conflict or cannot be verified, skip publication and report the reason.

entries.title: Turn a messy week of notes into a useful pediatrician question
entries.summary: A simple way to bring dates, context, and one clear question to an appointment.
entries.brief: Show how a log supports a conversation, not a diagnosis.
entries.appNote: If you use BabyBaby, the timeline can help you find the dates and entries you want to discuss at an appointment.

entries.title: A family routine that actually fits your family
entries.summary: A flexible way to notice what helps without trying to copy someone else's day.
entries.brief: Reflective and practical; no prescribed baby schedule. Optional memory note, no product pitch.
